primitives.name: Orinq receipts pallet
primitives.desc: Receipt registry with M-of-N committee attestation, availability certification, anchor records, attestor bonds and slashing, and fee escrow — the on-chain truth every other primitive commits to. Benchmarked threshold and non-threshold attestation paths return actual weights; conditional Currency calls refund unused MOTRA checkpoint budgets.

primitives.name: MOTRA fee resource
primitives.desc: Non-transferable transaction-fee resource generated from the lowest free MATRA held throughout each checkpoint interval (NIGHT/DUST model), with balance-change checkpoints preventing backdated funding and cycling, PalletId sovereign generation excluded, and a constant-cost legacy migration with an upgrade-block earning baseline. Gemtek Wasm benchmarks price checkpoint storage per touched account; runtime dispatch weights and initialization budgets cover Currency callers and batched transfers, with storage-observation property tests. Account creation does not write MOTRA state. Charged by a signed extension, with sponsor delegation for fresh accounts' first fees; the extension also gives a runtime-named (signer, call) set the top transaction-pool priority, one slot per signer, so the guardian's veto cannot be outbid for a place in a block. Retention and generated credit use bounded logarithmic conservative decay; the complete fee extension is benchmarked and refunds unused actual weight using the paid price. Committed Wasm samples pin checkpoint, reconciliation and fee weights.

primitives.name: Billing pallet
primitives.desc: Application-layer MATRA billing (pay_request) for API calls, metering and attestation evidence — the user-facing spend surface, distinct from MOTRA tx fees.

primitives.name: TEE attestation pallet
primitives.desc: Hardware attestation-evidence registry (secp256r1 and ARM TrustZone phone attestors) binding TEE quotes to receipts.

primitives.name: Committee seating gate
primitives.desc: Composed authority-selection gate: input sanitizer, dead-registered and dead-core liveness filters, seat-ramp clamp, live-quorum floor, growth-slack invariant, break-glass floor and pinned-committee override; refuses (keep-current) rather than seat a committee that cannot finalize, so a fresh chain keeps the genesis committee its chain spec declares until a quorum of Cardano's draw has authored. The author and every importing peer judge it on the same state: the runtime's check_inherents initialises the block first. Genesis refuses a chain spec whose committee is empty, has Aura or GRANDPA authorities seeded beside it, has more seats than MaxValidators, lists an authority twice or out of ascending cross-chain-key order, or gives two authorities one Aura or GRANDPA key.

primitives.name: Main-chain follower
primitives.desc: Cardano main-chain follower backends (db-sync and yaci-store with Mithril-certified stake) supplying candidate registrations and the D-parameter to authority selection.

primitives.name: Mainnet launch preflight
primitives.desc: Fail-closed genesis and launch gate: reads the raw chain spec, the runtime metadata extracted from its code, the authority launch commands (opening sh -c wrappers) and each authority's running node argv from a /proc/<pid>/cmdline capture, the nginx and cloudflared RPC proxy configs, each public RPC URL probed live over HTTP and a WebSocket, and Cardano mainnet through Kupo (the cMATRA genesis lock and its datum, and the permissioned candidates datum). Refuses on a well-known key anywhere (genesis, runtime code, any role or multisig member, the Cardano committee, node configs including dev-phrase URIs and the dev seed, the signing key), Sudo.Key or a genesis account no declared role accounts for, Root not a multisig two keyholders must sign for (one key that meets its threshold alone through a nested multisig counts as one keyholder) or one with a multisig at any depth of more members than the runtime's Multisig.MaxSignatories, which pallet_multisig never signs through, an undeclared off-chain role, a chain spec the anchor worker would read as a test network, attestor or validator reward parameters that are undeclared or not what genesis and the runtime hold, unsafe RPC on an authority, a public RPC URL that lists a method outside the safe set or answers an unsafe one, an authority with no launch entry, under-endowed attestors, genesis storage outside an allowlist, issuance plus the runtime's emission reserves above what the genesis lock holds, a lock fewer than two key holders can spend or not bound to this genesis, PerpEngine under any name, a runtime override or code substitute, a LastRuntimeUpgrade other than the spec version and name build-spec writes for the genesis code, a genesis-enabled Cardano deposit observation with no checkpoint, genesis, code, chain-spec and launch manifest hashes that differ from a manifest signed by a launch key the repo pins, a Root timelock guardian missing from genesis, not the declared multisig, not needing two keyholders or over MaxSignatories by the same test as Root, with a nested multisig member (whose veto the runtime does not take first), the sudo key or sharing any account or member with it, or timelock delays missing, below the runtime's mainnet delays, above its MaxDelay or out of order, both read from the runtime metadata; and hex in the raw spec, the manifests, the launch keys or the key tables in any spelling but the one its writer writes, or a JSON object in them that names a key twice, since the node reads another spelling as other bytes; and a number genesis stores (an attestor reward, the bond, the issuance, an account) at any width but its type's, or an account under any key but its own, which the node reads as zero or never reads; and an authority whose own node binary, pinned by sha256 and captured from its running process, run offline through export-blocks on its running argv's chain and database options, builds another genesis than the one the preflight computes, so any reading of the spec the preflight gets apart from the node shows as another hash, whose --chain names a chain built into the node or a file that is not the checked spec, or that runs another binary than the manifest pins; an authority whose running node serves another genesis as block 0 (its chain_getBlockHash 0, captured from its local RPC), as a node started on a database that already held one or on a spec file overwritten since does, or names another chain, chain type or properties than the checked spec (system_chain, system_chainType and system_properties), or whose --chain path (each directory on it and the file, by the ctime stat prints, against the process start /proc/<pid>/stat and /proc/stat give) changed less than a second before its node process started, since a node keeps the spec it read at its start; and an authority launch that runs a node subcommand other than build-spec or purge-chain before its node, since the others write a genesis into the base path; and a genesis committee (SessionCommitteeManagement.CurrentCommittee, which the runtime seats at every rotation whose Cardano draw fails, a fresh chain's first among them) that is not exactly the declared authorities' aura and grandpa key pairs, each once, is longer than the runtime's MaxValidators or serves an epoch other than 0, genesis Aura and GRANDPA authorities other than the declared keys, each once and every voter at weight 1, a genesis Grandpa.CurrentSetId other than 0 or a Grandpa.SetIdSession other than build-spec's set 0 in session 0, since a warp-synced node takes the runtime's set id, session validators other than the committee as the session genesis writes it, a filled pallet_session stub, two authorities that declare one key, a list length in more bytes than parity-scale-codec accepts, or a Cardano permissioned candidate's gran key other than the grandpa key the authority with its aura key declares, or a declared authority on no candidate, which the first committee drawn from Cardano leaves out; and genesis committee scripts whose candidate address is past the runtime's 120-byte MainchainAddress, which the runtime reads as all-zero policies, or is not UTF-8 or holds a NUL byte, which the node's follower panics on or cannot query; and a permissioned candidates datum (read, with the D-parameter, from the one unspent output holding each policy's token, in the formats the node's partner-chains v1.5.1 follower decodes) that holds a candidate Ariadne drops, repeats a key, or holds fewer than the two candidates the runtime draws a committee from, or a D-parameter that seats registered candidates, fewer permissioned seats than candidates, or more than MaxValidators; and a genesis Sidechain.SlotsPerEpoch other than the launch's declared slots_per_epoch, 0 (every block's initialization divides by it), or one whose sessions do not divide Cardano's epoch, as partner-chains' sidechain-slots requires; and an authority whose Cardano follower settings (the MC__ epoch layout, CARDANO_SECURITY_PARAMETER and CARDANO_ACTIVE_SLOTS_COEFF, from its env or anywhere in its launch) are missing or not, string for string, the launch's declared cardano_follower, or a declared set other than Cardano mainnet's, since a node on other settings than its peers' draws another committee or judges another Cardano block stable and refuses their committee changes and blocks.

primitives.name: Reproducible runtime build
primitives.desc: Builds a commit's runtime blob at a fixed path in a digest-pinned Rust image, with the runtime's build script remapping the toolchain, Cargo home and repository directories its panic messages name, so every builder gets the same bytes and code hash: the code a signed launch manifest pins can be rebuilt from source, and a genesis built from a plain spec carrying it does not depend on the node that ran build-spec.

primitives.name: Root timelock
primitives.desc: Holds every non-exempt Root call for a per-class delay (recovery for committee toggles and delay raises, the standard delay for everything else including consensus-key levers, sudo key rotation and kill-switch restarts unless the guardian co-signs, long for the dedicated bridge and supply levers) in a bounded vetoable queue with a guardian veto, bulk veto, fast-track and a one-shot advance approval that Root runs without a queue place, plus one guardian change the guardian cannot veto and the sudo key can withdraw; the runtime call filter lets the sudo key reach Root at once only for pause, withdrawal and session-bounded finality break-glass calls, for scheduling and for the approved call, each timelock call is charged for every call its classifier walks, and genesis refuses a chain spec without an independent guardian, or with a development account as guardian, and allows an unguarded one only when its sudo key is a development account or absent. Its mainnet delays (DefaultDelays) and their ceiling (MaxDelay) are metadata constants, so a genesis audit can bound the stored delays from the runtime alone. The guardian's veto and co-sign calls (cancel, cancel_all, fast_track, approve), signed by the current guardian directly or through a multisig as_multi wrapper, are given the top transaction-pool priority through the MOTRA fee extension, bounded to one slot per signer and to the wrapped call's own weight, so a stolen sudo key cannot buy its way past the veto and a compromised guardian cannot use the priority to fill blocks.

primitives.name: Seat-key probe
primitives.desc: Lists the session keys a running validator's keystore names, with no unsafe RPC: finds every process with an authority flag, tells its chain by the database it holds open, refuses dev keys held in memory, and walks to the keystore in the node's own root without following a link. Its named set is an upper bound that never leaves out a key the node can sign with, so it can refuse a seat named on two hosts but never prove a host signs; positive claims come from chain evidence.

primitives.name: Native ZK and hybrid MATRA specification
primitives.desc: Phase-aware PREPROD native ZK acceptance harness with a real Rust driver, namespace-isolated core tests and dependency negative control, source-derived mainnet file-route refusal, actual runtime metadata compatibility and mutants, Aiken codec evaluation and measured no_std Sapling Wasm verification. --full always validates the lock and unit tests, selecting phases through CURRENT_PHASE only for ZK/spec changes against FPL_DIFF_BASE or the origin/main merge-base; --all retains every end-state check regardless of paths. CI filters ZK, spec, harness, runtime, pallet and chain-spec paths; the Sapling spike and independently rebuilt runtime metadata comparison, pinned to partnerchain/Cargo.lock, run only for ZK/spec changes. The required Rust workflow has no P0 baseline gate. Mainnet, spend and external commitments remain denied.

primitives.name: Native ZK bridge recipient codec
primitives.desc: Standalone canonical v1 Account and Utxo CBOR recipient codecs in no_std Rust and Aiken, with actual CEK evaluator round trips and refusal of reserved Shielded, unknown version/tag/lock, malformed length, trailing bytes and noncanonical integers. P0 primitive only; no deployed bridge or value activation.

primitives.name: Native ZK Sapling verification core
primitives.desc: Experimental no_std Sapling verification core using arkworks Groth16/BLS12-381 and upstream Sapling/Jubjub signatures and tree primitives. Rust 1.85.0 wasm32 build, pinned real Zcash mainnet corpus, exhaustive proof-bit mutations and public-input controls that reject a pairing-result bypass and complete one-spend/two-output bundle measurements. Standalone P0 feasibility primitive; no runtime pool, value activation or reviewed slowest-hardware claim.
